header:
Date: 2026-12-28 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood CSM); Ruth Barnes (Elm CTO), Diego Morales (Lead ML Engineer), Hannah Liu (Platform Engineer), Priya Singh (Product)
summary: POC scoping call focused on integration planning for Elm Analytics. Main goals: agree success criteria, validate workload sizing, define benchmark plan, and outline SDK/OpenAI-compatible integration approach (including tool/function calling and structured outputs). Security and network constraints (VPC, KMS) discussed. Next steps: send integration guide, run baseline benchmarks on Elm sample set, schedule deeper private deployment demo, and share security docs.
topics: Tool/function calling and structured output schemas
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Patel: okay, thanks everyone for joining, um it's Jordan from Redwood, i'll run quick intro then hand over to avery for the SE side 00:06 Ruth Barnes: hi thanks, appreciate it, we are excited to see how this could replace our current inference path 00:12 Avery Chen: awesome, quick agenda - success criteria, workload sizing, what you need to integrate (SDKs, openai-compatible endpoints), benchmarks and timelines. feel free to interrupt. 00:22 Priya Singh: sounds good. 00:30 Diego Morales: quick context - we run embeddings plus generation for a document QA app; typical steady qps is about 30 qps embedding calls, generation bursts up to 120 tokens/sec-ish across 6 workers, and peak traffic during business hours maybe 60 qps for embeddings. latency targets are sub-300ms for embeddings and sub-800ms for generation if possible. 00:48 Jordan Patel: great, that's helpful; can you say what models you're using today and where it's hosted? 00:54 Diego Morales: right now we call openai's davinci-ish endpoints for generation and ada for embeddings via a managed provider; we also have some on-prem GPU spares but not production-ready. 01:06 Maya Lopez: and your success criteria - is it purely latency/cost, or also quality/regression gating? 01:12 Ruth Barnes: all three. primary is reducing per-call cost by at least 30% while keeping quality within our eval set thresholds. also need SSO/SCIM and SOC2-level compliance. 01:24 Samir Rao: okay noted - so success criteria = cost delta >=30% and quality within x% of your current F1 on the benchmark, plus security questionnaire answers. 01:33 Priya Singh: timeline - we're aiming for a pilot with real traffic in Q1; ideally a 6-week pilot starting mid-Jan. 01:40 Jordan Patel: that's doable. let's talk integration approach - Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints and SDKs in python/js, and we support function/tool calling patterns. for private deployments we can expose a drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint in a VPC. 01:57 Hannah Liu: question - when you say OpenAI-compatible, does that include the function-calling spec and the same request/response shapes? 02:04 Avery Chen: yes - we implement the common function-calling pattern and structured outputs; we do have some differences around streaming chunk boundaries sometimes, and model names differ, but the payload shapes are compatible enough to reuse client code. 02:16 Diego Morales: nice. on structured outputs, we need strict JSON schema outputs for downstream ingestion - can you guarantee stable schema across model versions during a pilot? 02:26 Maya Lopez: we provide best-effort model pinning - you can pin a model version for the pilot and we'll lock rollout. for longer terms we recommend evaluation rails; but during a pilot we can pin the version so schema drift is minimized. 02:37 Ruth Barnes: good, we will want KV cache behavior explained - we saw weird cold-start latencies before. 02:44 Avery Chen: yes automatic kv/prefix cache reduces per-token compute; cold starts still happen on new prefixes but we can instrument and surface token-level latency breakdowns in the console. 02:55 Diego Morales: benchmark plan - we want to run a baseline against OpenAI and Redwood to compare latency and cost for our 3 sample prompts plus embeddings. 03:04 Jordan Patel: recommended: we run two scenarios - steady throughput (30 qps embeddings + 10 qps gen) and peak burst (120 qps gen bursts). we'll instrument end-to-end latency and cost per 1k tokens. 03:16 Priya Singh: what about security and keys? we require KMS integration and audit logs retained 1 year. 03:23 Samir Rao: we have KMS integrations (aws/gcp/azure) and can enable audit log export to your SIEM. SOC2 docs are ready to share. we'll send those after the call. 03:33 Hannah Liu: on networking - if we do private, we need a VPC peering or private link. do you support self-hosted control plane? 03:41 Avery Chen: yes, we offer private with customer-managed networking; options include VPC peering, private link, or an on-prem bundle in air-gapped setups. 03:51 Diego Morales: for benchmarking we need realistic cost numbers - are there quantization profiles we can test to lower cost? 03:58 Maya Lopez: yes we can test INT8 and 4-bit quantized variants depending on model family; Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles, and SE will include recommended profiles in the benchmark plan. 04:10 Ruth Barnes: any blockers on our side for a quick pilot? 04:14 Hannah Liu: we need to confirm identity provider SAML details and a contact for network setup. 04:19 Jordan Patel: ok next steps are Jordan will send pricing/pilot terms and a short integration guide demonstrating OpenAI-compatible python/js snippets, Avery will kick off the benchmark plan and request the sample prompts/data, and Hannah will share network diagram. 04:33 Diego Morales: on data residency - our data cannot leave EU for this pilot. 04:37 Avery Chen: understood - we have regional endpoints in eu-west and can route requests accordingly; for private we can deploy in your EU region. 04:45 Priya Singh: one more thing - function/tool calling: we plan to call internal tools (retrieval, RAG orchestration), do you support tool auth and arbitrary tool chaining? 04:56 Maya Lopez: we support function-calling hooks and can attach signed tool credentials; orchestration patterns are possible but often customers put orchestration in their platform and call Redwood for model inferencing only. we can show example patterns in the integration guide. 05:10 Diego Morales: great. on acceptance criteria - we'll define pass if: cost <=70% of current, average embedding latency <300ms, generation 95th perc <1s, outputs match schema for 90% of golden set. 05:22 Jordan Patel: that's a good starting set; we'll add those to the pilot SLO doc. 05:27 Hannah Liu: what's the expected time to stand up a private endpoint? 05:30 Avery Chen: typically 2-3 weeks for VPC setup and control plane prep, + 1 week for model pinning and benchmark runs - overall pilot could start mid-Jan if we move fast. 05:41 Ruth Barnes: ok let's do it. Jordan, please send the guide and pricing and we'll get the internal approvals. 05:47 Jordan Patel: will do - thanks everyone. 05:50 Priya Singh: thanks, bye. 05:52 [call ends]
